title: Optical spin injection in graphane and fluorographene
authors: Angélica Marina López-Martínez, César Castillo-Quevedo, Cesar Camas-Flores, Analila Luna-Valenzuela, Jose Luis Cabellos
abstract: We theoretically investigate the optical spin-injection response in different stoichiometric configurations of graphane and fluorographene using density functional theory. Our goal is to determine which configuration yields the strongest degree of spin polarization. The results show that the fluorographene zigzag configuration yields the best degree of spin polarization response (${\cal DSP}^{\mathrm{z}}$), with 98\% spin polarized electrons at the band edge and over a wide range of excitation photon energies. In contrast, other graphane and fluorographene configurations achieve a ${\cal DSP}^{\mathrm{z}}$ of roughly 83--100\%, but only within a limited photon-excitation energy range. In structures with low spin-orbit coupling, the degree of spin polarization is close to 100\% over a wide range of photon energies. For higher spin-orbit coupling, this strong response appears, but only in a narrow photon energy region. Additionally, under the band-resolved decomposition scheme, the contributions of different band-to-band transitions to the ${\cal DSP}^{\mathrm{z}}$ spectrum are identified by summing only the selected valence and conduction bands. Our findings show that almost the entire ${\cal DSP}^{\mathrm{z}}$ spectrum of the fluorographene zigzag configuration comes from transitions that involve only the top valence band, which is a mixture of C--p and F--p states.
summary: The research uses DFT calculations to model optical spin injection efficiency in graphane and fluorographene structures. It determines that the fluorographene zigzag configuration offers superior spin polarization ($	ext{DSP}_z$) over a broad energy range compared to other tested geometries. This highlights how controlled functionalization of 2D carbon materials can be engineered for advanced spintronic applications.
main_problem: The study theoretically investigates the optical spin-injection response in various stoichiometric configurations of graphane and fluorographene to determine which structure yields the strongest degree of spin polarization for spintronic applications.
main_result: The fluorographene zigzag configuration was found to yield the best spin polarization ($	ext{DSP}_z$), achieving 98% polarization over a wide range of excitation energies, while other configurations showed limitations in energy bandwidth or lower polarization.
method: Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations were employed using the ABINIT package to compute the optical spin-injection spectrum ($	ext{DSP}_z$) based on one-photon transition amplitudes derived from linear optical response tensors.
model_or_system: The physical systems are graphene derivatives: graphane (hydrogenated) and fluorographene (fluorinated), examined across four geometric configurations (chair, boat, zigzag, armchair). The analysis focuses on the electronic structure modifications due to $	ext{H}$ or $	ext{F}$ functionalization.
key_observables: Degree of Spin Polarization ($	ext{DSP}_z$), spin-polarized electron density at the band edge, and the energy range over which this polarization is maintained.
important_parameters: Spin-Orbit Coupling (SOC) strength, excitation photon energy ($\hbar\omega$), and structural distortion relative to pristine graphene.
main_assumptions: The theory relies on a one-photon transition amplitude approximation; calculations use the PBE functional within GGA and neglect non-linear core corrections or excitonic effects.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the geometric configurations (chair, boat, zigzag, armchair) and display the calculated $	ext{DSP}_z$ spectra as a function of photon energy for both graphane and fluorographene.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the electronic structure and spin-polarization response ($	ext{DSP}_z$) across all four geometric motifs for both hydrogenated (graphane) and fluorinated (fluorographene) graphene, comparing results based on SOC strength and structural distortion.
why_interesting: This work is relevant because it models spin injection in 2D materials using first-principles methods, providing insights into how chemical functionalization ($	ext{H}$ vs $	ext{F}$) can tune electronic properties for spintronic devices, which relates to open quantum systems dynamics.

Spintronics.note: The new paper directly investigates 'optical spin-injection' and calculates the degree of spin polarization ($\text{DSP}_z$) in carbon nanostructures for spintronic applications, which aligns perfectly with the scope of quantum-optics concepts applied to spin transport.
